system_prompt:
You are a QA tester for a small web app. Use only the browser tools you are given and behave like a real user: open pages, read them, type into fields and click buttons. Never run JavaScript in the page. After every navigation take a fresh page snapshot before typing or clicking, and after clicking a button wait about one second, then take another snapshot so you read the message the page shows. The login page has a username field, a password field and a log in button; the result appears in the status area under the form. The chat page is at /chat, is only available after logging in, and shows sent messages in the chat log or an error under the form. Type text exactly as given, including empty values. Decide whether the form ACCEPTED the input (valid: a welcome message, or the chat message appearing in the chat log) or REJECTED it (invalid: an error message). Use as few steps as possible and do not retry. Your final answer must end with exactly one line in this format and nothing after it:
VERDICT: valid|invalid | <exact message shown on the page>
For an accepted chat message use the text that appeared in the chat log as the message.

cases.name: valid_login
cases.instruction: Open the login page and log in as demo_user with the password ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD}. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: wrong_password
cases.instruction: Open the login page and try to log in as demo_user with the password not-the-right-one. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: unknown_username
cases.instruction: Open the login page and try to log in as ghost_user (a user that does not exist) with the password ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD}. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: empty_username
cases.instruction: Open the login page, leave the username field empty, type ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD} as the password and press the log in button. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: empty_password
cases.instruction: Open the login page, type demo_user as the username, leave the password field empty and press the log in button. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: injection_username
cases.instruction: Open the login page and try to log in with this exact username: ' OR '1'='1 and this exact password: ' OR '1'='1 . This is an SQL injection attempt that the app must reject. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: deliberate_fail_demo
cases.instruction: Open the login page and try to log in as demo_user with the password not-the-right-one. Report whether the login succeeded.

cases.name: chat_valid_message
cases.instruction: First log in on the login page as demo_user with the password ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD}. Then open the chat page and send this message: Hello, I need an appointment on Monday. Report whether the message was accepted.

cases.name: chat_empty_message
cases.instruction: First log in on the login page as demo_user with the password ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD}. Then open the chat page, leave the message field empty and press the send button. Report whether the message was accepted.

cases.name: chat_too_long_message
cases.instruction: First log in on the login page as demo_user with the password ${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD}. Then open the chat page and send this exact message of 201 characters (the letter a 201 times): aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa . Report whether the message was accepted.
